children: A California district court judge rejected Walmart’s
bid to dismiss a lawsuit brought by Estée Lauder
, ruling that the retail giant could face claims that it sold counterfeit cosmetics and even expanding the scope of the case beyond the 17 products tested for authenticity.

for facilitating the sale of counterfeit versions of its licensed products by its namesake banner, La Mer, Le Labo, Clinique, Aveda, and Tom Ford. The counterfeit items were sold by third parties on Walmart’s website.

“This is readily apparent given the [counterfeits] were permitted to be sold on Defendants’ website despite their stated careful selection process of whom they choose as a Marketplace seller/partner,” Estée Lauder’s complaint states.

to further profit from these sales.
After confirming 17 items tested were not manufactured by Estée Lauder, the judge on the case determined that not only could the lawsuit against Walmart
proceed, but it could also be extended beyond those 17 items.

complaint lacked factual allegations tying the retailer to other products sold by third-party sellers on Walmart.com and that the products were not sufficiently related to warrant inclusion in a single suit.

However, Judge Hernan Vera ruled that Walmart’s request for a dismissal is “unjustified at this stage” and opened the opportunity for Estée Lauder to expand its lawsuit beyond the 17 products tested for authenticity.

title: Judge gives Estée Lauder green light to expand counterfeit lawsuit against Walmart
